title: Modal verbs 6: would (past habits)
note: RESCOPED 2026-09-02 from the parked duplicate of a2_used_to. WOULD for repeated past actions: We would go swimming every summer. USED TO stays whole at a2_used_to - do not re-teach it. The one rule that matters: would does NOT work with states (*I would have a dog), only used to does. Items therefore contrast the two rather than drilling would alone. Thickened 11 -> 25 items 2026-09-04 (agent loop): 14 new, 8 would-actions and 6 used-to states, so the contrast is drilled from both sides. Rules applied this pass: A8 contraction twins closed (5 items - would + pronoun contracts to 'd); A4 the lake / in the park / in the snow rewritten onto sentences that need no article (go swimming, go skiing, play football); F3 stories / Christmas / quite / snowman swapped for taught words. A0 fork - Czech Kazde leto jsme jezdili is *would go*, *used to go* AND *went*, so on every would item the used to twin is in gap_accepts and accepts; the Quiz options are what force would, and they carry this unit's own errors (would to go, would went, used to going). State items stay determinate, because would is simply wrong there. Queued in DECISIONS.md. Remaining lint: vocablevel only.

cards.title: Modal verbs 6: would (past habits)
points: **would** here is not a wish. It means: this happened many times, and it stopped.

rows: something you did again and again

examples.en: My grandfather **would** tell us a story.

cards.title: Actions yes, states no
points: A **state** is not something you did — it is something that was true.

cards.title: It needs a time frame
points: Start with **when I** was… or **every…** so the habit reading is clear.

rows: When I was a child, I **would** walk to school.
*when I was a child* sets it
on its own this sounds like a wish, not a habit

cards.title: Common mistakes
points: **would** takes a plain verb, and never a state verb.

items.en: We would go swimming every summer.
accepts: We would go swimming every summer.
We used to go swimming every summer.
We'd go swimming every summer.
items.wrong: We would to go swimming every summer.
items.explanation: **would** + the plain verb **go**. *Every summer* makes it a repeated habit.
items.explanation_cz: **would** + základní tvar **go**. *Every summer* z toho dělá opakovaný zvyk.

items.en: My grandfather would tell us a story every evening.
items.cz: Dědeček nám každý večer vyprávěl příběh.
items.gap: My grandfather ____ us a story every evening. (tell)
accepts: My grandfather would tell us a story every evening.
My grandfather used to tell us a story every evening.
items.explanation: **would** takes the plain verb: would **tell**, never would told.
items.explanation_cz: Po **would** je základní tvar: would **tell**, nikdy would told.
items.wrong: My grandfather would told us a story every evening.

items.en: I used to have a dog.
accepts: I used to have a dog.
items.wrong: I would have a dog.
items.explanation: **have** is a state here, so only **used to** works — not would.
items.explanation_cz: **have** je tady stav, takže funguje jen **used to** — ne would.

items.en: She used to be a teacher.
accepts: She used to be a teacher.
items.wrong: She would be a teacher.
items.explanation: **be** is a state. States take **used to**, never would.
items.explanation_cz: **be** je stav. Stavy mají **used to**, nikdy would.

items.en: When I was a child, I would walk to school.
items.cz: Když jsem byl malý, chodil jsem do školy pěšky.
items.gap: When I was a child, I ____ to school. (walk)
accepts: When I was a child, I would walk to school.
When I was a child, I used to walk to school.
When I was a child, I'd walk to school.
items.explanation: *When I was a child* sets the frame, so **would** walk reads as a habit.
items.explanation_cz: *When I was a child* dává rámec, takže **would** walk zní jako zvyk.

items.en: We would visit my aunt every Sunday.
items.cz: Každou neděli jsme jezdili za tetou.
accepts: We would visit my aunt every Sunday.
We used to visit my aunt every Sunday.
We'd visit my aunt every Sunday.
items.explanation: **visit** is a repeated action, so **would** visit is fine.
items.explanation_cz: **visit** je opakovaná činnost, takže **would** visit je v pořádku.
items.wrong: We would visited my aunt every Sunday.

items.en: I used to know him very well.
items.cz: Dřív jsem ho znal moc dobře.
accepts: I used to know him very well.
items.wrong: I would know him very well.
items.explanation: **know** is a state — **used to** only.
items.explanation_cz: **know** je stav — jen **used to**.

items.en: My father would read to us every night.
items.gap: My father ____ to us every night. (read)
accepts: My father would read to us every night.
My father used to read to us every night.
items.explanation: *Every night* plus the action **read** gives you **would** read.
items.explanation_cz: *Every night* a činnost **read** dávají **would** read.

items.en: They used to live in Ostrava.
accepts: They used to live in Ostrava.
items.explanation: **live** describes a state of affairs, so **used to** is the safe one here.
items.explanation_cz: **live** popisuje stav, takže **used to** je tu ta bezpečná volba.

items.en: Every winter we would go skiing.
accepts: Every winter we would go skiing.
Every winter we used to go skiing.
Every winter we'd go skiing.
items.explanation: *Every winter* gives the repeat, and **go** stays plain: **would go**.
items.explanation_cz: *Every winter* dává opakování a **go** zůstává základní: **would go**.
items.wrong: Every winter we would went skiing.

items.en: I used to like coffee, but now I don't.
items.cz: Dřív mi chutnala káva, ale teď ne.
items.gap: I ____ coffee, but now I don't. (like)
accepts: I used to like coffee, but now I don't.
I used to like coffee, but now I do not.
items.wrong: I would like coffee, but now I don't.
items.explanation: **like** is a state. Note that *I would like* means something else entirely.
items.explanation_cz: **like** je stav. Pozor: *I would like* znamená něco úplně jiného.

items.en: When I was a student, I would work at weekends.
items.cz: Když jsem studoval, o víkendech jsem pracoval.
items.gap: When I was a student, I ____ at weekends. (work)
accepts: When I was a student, I would work at weekends.
When I was a student, I used to work at weekends.
When I was a student, I'd work at weekends.
items.wrong: When I was a student, I would worked at weekends.
items.explanation: *When I was a student* sets the frame, so **would** work reads as a repeated habit.
items.explanation_cz: *When I was a student* dává rámec, takže **would** work zní jako opakovaný zvyk.

items.en: My mother would cook a big lunch every Sunday.
items.cz: Máma každou neděli vařila velký oběd.
items.gap: My mother ____ a big lunch every Sunday. (cook)
accepts: My mother would cook a big lunch every Sunday.
My mother used to cook a big lunch every Sunday.
items.wrong: My mother would cooking a big lunch every Sunday.
items.explanation: **would** is followed by the plain verb **cook** — no -ing, no -ed.
items.explanation_cz: Po **would** je základní tvar **cook** — žádné -ing ani -ed.

items.en: They would play football after school every day.
items.cz: Po škole si každý den hráli fotbal.
items.gap: They ____ football after school every day. (play)
accepts: They would play football after school every day.
They used to play football after school every day.
They'd play football after school every day.
items.wrong: They would to play football after school every day.
items.explanation: There is no **to** after would: **would play**.
items.explanation_cz: Po would není žádné **to**: **would play**.

items.en: He would drive us to school every morning.
items.cz: Každé ráno nás vozil do školy.
items.gap: He ____ us to school every morning. (drive)
accepts: He would drive us to school every morning.
He used to drive us to school every morning.
He'd drive us to school every morning.
items.wrong: He would drove us to school every morning.
items.explanation: **drive** stays plain after would: **would drive**, not would drove.
items.explanation_cz: Po would zůstává **drive** v základním tvaru: **would drive**, ne would drove.

items.en: We would meet in a small cafe every Friday.
items.cz: Každý pátek jsme se scházeli v malé kavárně.
items.gap: We ____ in a small cafe every Friday. (meet)
accepts: We would meet in a small cafe every Friday.
We used to meet in a small cafe every Friday.
We'd meet in a small cafe every Friday.
items.wrong: We would met in a small cafe every Friday.
items.explanation: *Every Friday* makes it a habit, and **meet** stays plain: **would meet**.
items.explanation_cz: *Every Friday* z toho dělá zvyk a **meet** zůstává v základním tvaru: **would meet**.

items.en: After dinner we would go for a walk.
items.cz: Po večeři jsme chodili na procházku.
items.gap: After dinner we ____ for a walk. (go)
accepts: After dinner we would go for a walk.
After dinner we used to go for a walk.
After dinner we'd go for a walk.
items.wrong: After dinner we would went for a walk.
items.explanation: **go** keeps its plain form after would: **would go**.
items.explanation_cz: **go** si po would drží základní tvar: **would go**.

items.en: When I was a child, my father would take me to work.
items.cz: Když jsem byl malý, táta mě brával do práce.
items.gap: When I was a child, my father ____ me to work. (take)
accepts: When I was a child, my father would take me to work.
When I was a child, my father used to take me to work.
items.wrong: When I was a child, my father would took me to work.
items.explanation: **take** stays plain: **would take**. The frame is *when I was a child*.
items.explanation_cz: **take** zůstává základní: **would take**. Rámec je *when I was a child*.

items.en: My brother would help me with my homework.
items.gap: My brother ____ me with my homework. (help)
accepts: My brother would help me with my homework.
My brother used to help me with my homework.
items.wrong: My brother would helped me with my homework.
items.explanation: **help** is a repeated action, so **would help** — plain verb, no -ed.
items.explanation_cz: **help** je opakovaná činnost, takže **would help** — základní tvar, žádné -ed.

items.en: I used to be afraid of dogs.
accepts: I used to be afraid of dogs.
items.wrong: I would be afraid of dogs.
items.explanation: Being afraid is a **state**, not something you did again and again — so **used to**, never would.
items.explanation_cz: Strach je **stav**, ne něco, co jsi opakovaně dělal — proto **used to**, nikdy would.

items.en: She used to have long hair.
accepts: She used to have long hair.
items.wrong: She would have long hair.
items.explanation: **have** is a state here — hair is not an action. Only **used to** works.
items.explanation_cz: **have** je tady stav — vlasy nejsou činnost. Funguje jen **used to**.

items.en: She used to want to be a doctor.
accepts: She used to want to be a doctor.
items.wrong: She would want to be a doctor.
items.explanation: **want** is a state verb. States take **used to**, and never the -ing form.
items.explanation_cz: **want** je stavové sloveso. Stavy mají **used to** a nikdy tvar na -ing.

items.en: He used to understand German.
accepts: He used to understand German.
items.wrong: He would understand German.
items.explanation: **understand** is a state — you cannot repeat it like an action, so **used to**.
items.explanation_cz: **understand** je stav — nedá se opakovat jako činnost, proto **used to**.

items.en: We used to have a small garden.
accepts: We used to have a small garden.
items.wrong: We would have a small garden.
items.explanation: Owning a garden is a **state**. *We would have* would mean something else entirely.
items.explanation_cz: Vlastnit zahradu je **stav**. *We would have* by znamenalo něco úplně jiného.

items.en: She used to know my sister.
accepts: She used to know my sister.
items.wrong: She would know my sister.
items.explanation: **know** is a state, so **used to know**. *She would know* is a guess about now.
items.explanation_cz: **know** je stav, proto **used to know**. *She would know* je odhad o přítomnosti.
